question: The ratio of the efficiencies of two workers, P and Q, is 5 : 2. If P can complete a project in 12 days, how many days will Q take to complete the same project alone?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time and efficiency are inversely proportional to each other.

Ratio of Time taken by P and Q = 2 : 5

Here, 2 parts correspond to 12 days.

So, 1 part = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 days.

Time taken by Q (5 parts) = 5 × 6 = 30 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of the efficiencies of P and Q = 5 : 2

Time taken by P to complete the project = 12 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

Time = Total Work ÷ Efficiency

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the efficiency of P be 5 units/day and Q be 2 units/day.

⇒ Total Work = Efficiency of P × Time taken by P

⇒ Total Work = 5 × 12 = 60 units

⇒ Time taken by Q = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of Q

⇒ Time taken by Q = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 days

**∴ The correct answer is 30 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Time and Efficiency Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a work. If the ratio of efficiencies of A and B is x : y, then the ratio of time taken by them is y : x.

Combined Work Rule

If A can do a piece of work in x days and B can do it in y days, their combined efficiency is (1/x + 1/y). Together they complete the work in (x × y) ÷ (x + y) days.

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in proportion to the total work done by each person. If workers work for the exact same number of days, wages are distributed in the direct ratio of their efficiencies.
